status_legend.VERIFIED: Acceptance is directly exercised through the relevant public or persisted path.
status_legend.PARTIAL: A material portion is exercised, but an end-to-end, fault-injection, or external authority condition remains unproven.
status_legend.UNSUPPORTED: No adequate executable evidence was produced in this remediation shard.

T13.evidence: Existing typed artifacts are verified and rebound to trial, split, fidelity, objective and evidence before use.

T14.evidence: FAILED/PRUNED and quality-pruned COMPLETE artifacts cannot update the incumbent.

T15.evidence: Issued jobs bind tier, recipe and attempt; replay is idempotent and the real runner visits the declared tiers.

T16.evidence: Technical COMPLETE without an authoritative quality decision is pruned at the cheap tier.

T17.evidence: FA final-fidelity gates and FO receipt binding prevent lower-fidelity evidence from becoming the final winner.

T18.evidence: Plateau orientation is derived from the objective direction, including minimize.

T19.evidence: Fixed-reference hypervolume replaces frontier-count semantics; exact two-old-points-to-one-strong-point geometry and the runner progress trace are exercised.

T20.evidence: Final uncertainty controls replacement and an adversarial point-dominant volatile candidate cannot eliminate the conservative legal winner.

T26.evidence: Production QE runs with permuted candidate columns, independent single columns, and factor shards use one common resampling plan. Canonical identity alignment yields one candidate-set hash and identical FA decision IDs/content hashes after FO receipt verification.

T27.evidence: A production frozen fitted FP recipe produces an unchanged historical prefix after future-tail perturbation. Under the same fit, plan, and comparison context, production QE evidence, candidate identities, and the FO-verified FA decision remain identical; labels are not inputs to the causal path.

T28.evidence: The actual runner fully evaluates parent, both split branches, and recombined candidate; the durable store retains all four under one campaign and binds one complete family to the sealed runner ledger.

T30.evidence: FO and FP replay the exact same canonical FA provider/request and receive identical decision_id and content_hash.

T89.evidence: On the same execution device, one batch and repeated differently sized batches aggregate by preregistered hypothesis identity and produce the identical complete-family artifact and correction result under one fixed ledger head/count.

T90.evidence: Pending/failed slots remain in the typed family and FO rejects member-set truncation.

T91.evidence: Multiplicity reduces lifecycle events to terminal proposal outcomes; SELECTED/PROPOSED do not inflate proposals.

T92.evidence: PRUNED, INVALID, SELECTED and resumed ledger histories finish with reconcilable counts.

T93.evidence: CLOSED and SEALED state survives serialization; authorized extension retains prior epoch seals.

T94.evidence: Head/count/next-sequence truncation checks and crash injection immediately before and after sealing verify deterministic finish recovery.

T95.evidence: V2 canonical named-field JSON distinguishes delimiter-collision records.

T96.evidence: JSON retains null/string types; hash encoding is versioned and V1 ledgers remain readable without claiming V2 identity.

T111.evidence: Actual QE common-plan bootstrap feeds one FA provider/request; direct FA, FO final path and FP adapter return identical decision/content hashes. Legacy local scoring cannot be invoked as default authority and explicit screening results are marked non-authoritative.

T112.evidence: Two durable worker attempt identities increase operation count while collapsing to one effective hypothesis; the first validation p-value survives restart and the complete retry family binds to a sealed ledger.

T115.evidence: Screening-only COMPLETE scores cannot become selectable fitness, missing qualification yields no utility, and local treatment ranking is explicitly labeled screening diagnostic rather than formal authority.

T166.evidence: A callback fails after 9 of 10 synthetic work units; the durable runner charges the full reserved envelope, consumes one evaluation, and exposes no replacement budget. This is deliberately a conservative upper-bound charge, not a claim of measured worker utilization.

T167.evidence: Actual overrun is recorded rather than refunded, and the exhausted budget prevents later dispatch.

T168.evidence: Unstarted cancellation releases; started failure commits cost under an attempt identity.

T169.evidence: Settlement/release resolves an exact attempt; duplicate or mismatched operations cannot consume another reservation.

T170.evidence: A missing-worker reservation remains charged after durable restart and checkpoint restore, replacement dispatch cannot enlarge the budget, and a checkpoint that drops the orphan attempt identity while retaining aggregate reservations is rejected.

T171.evidence: SQLite transactions and in-memory locks serialize state changes, and a dedicated concurrent settle-versus-cancel race proves one exact attempt cannot be consumed twice.

cross_chain_limitations: Synthetic qualification receipts are explicitly test-scoped and prove wiring only; they are not production numerical certification.
Worker migration and physical 90%-completion metering require external execution infrastructure and are not claimed from isolated unit tests.
Synthetic and local concurrency tests validate state-machine behavior but do not substitute for production multi-host failure injection.
